blocks.label: [A]
blocks.title: Urban Heat Islands
blocks.body:
Cities are often several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside, a phenomenon known as the urban heat island effect. Materials such as asphalt and concrete absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night. In addition, cities have fewer trees and plants, which cool the air by releasing water through their leaves. As a result, urban areas ( 19 ).
This extra heat is more than just uncomfortable. During heat waves, it can increase the risk of heatstroke, especially for elderly people who live alone. It also raises electricity use, as people turn up their air conditioners, which in turn ( 20 ). Some researchers describe this as a vicious cycle.
To address the problem, cities are experimenting with a variety of solutions. Some have painted roofs white to reflect sunlight, while others have planted trees along streets and created rooftop gardens. ( 21 ), not all solutions work equally well in every climate. White roofs, for example, can increase heating costs in places with cold winters, so city planners must consider local conditions carefully.

o: cool down more quickly at night
often stay hot even after sunset
receive less sunlight than rural areas
get more rain than the countryside
qs.ex: 昼に熱をため夜にゆっくり放出し、植物も少ない → 日没後も暑いままになりがちです。

o: releases more heat into the streets
qs.ex: エアコンの排熱がさらに街を暑くする「悪循環(vicious cycle)」です。
さまざまな対策がある → しかし、どの気候でも同じように効くわけではない、という逆接です。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: Sleep and Memory
blocks.body:
For a long time, sleep was thought to be a passive state in which the brain simply rested. However, research over the past few decades has shown that the brain is highly active during sleep, and that sleep plays an important role in ( 22 ).
In one well-known type of experiment, participants learn a task, such as a list of word pairs, and are tested on it later. Those who sleep between learning and testing usually perform better than those who stay awake for the same amount of time. Scientists believe that during sleep, the brain ( 23 ), strengthening important information and transferring it to long-term storage.
These findings have practical implications for students. Staying up all night to study before an exam may seem like a good use of time, but it can actually be counterproductive. ( 24 ), spreading study sessions over several days and getting enough sleep each night is likely to lead to better results.

qs.ex: 以降の段落で、睡眠と記憶の定着について説明しています。
重要な情報を強化し長期記憶へ移す、という説明につながります。
徹夜は逆効果 → そうではなく(Instead)、数日に分けて勉強し十分に寝るほうがよい。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.title: Fuel for a Greener Sky
blocks.body:
Air travel connects people and economies around the world, but it comes at an environmental cost. Aviation is responsible for roughly 2 to 3 percent of global carbon dioxide emissions, and that share is expected to grow as more people fly. Unlike cars, large passenger planes cannot easily be powered by batteries, because batteries heavy enough to carry a plane across an ocean would be far too heavy to lift off the ground. For this reason, many experts see sustainable aviation fuel, or SAF, as the most realistic way to reduce emissions in the near future.
SAF is produced from materials such as used cooking oil, agricultural waste, and even household garbage. When it is burned, it releases about as much carbon dioxide as ordinary jet fuel. However, because the plants and waste used to make it absorbed carbon dioxide from the atmosphere as they grew, SAF can reduce emissions over its entire life cycle by up to 80 percent, depending on how it is produced. Another advantage is that SAF can be mixed with regular fuel and used in existing aircraft without major changes to their engines.
Despite these benefits, SAF currently makes up less than 1 percent of the jet fuel used worldwide. The biggest obstacle is cost: SAF is often two to three times more expensive than conventional fuel, and the supply of suitable raw materials is limited. To encourage production, governments have begun to act. The European Union, for example, requires that a gradually increasing percentage of the fuel supplied at its airports be SAF, and Japan has set a goal of replacing 10 percent of the fuel used by its airlines with SAF by 2030. Whether such policies will be enough to make SAF affordable remains to be seen.

qs.q: Why do many experts believe SAF is important for aviation?
o: Electric planes are already common on long flights.
Batteries are currently too heavy to power large planes over long distances.
Jet fuel will soon be impossible to produce.
Airlines want to make flights cheaper.
qs.ex: 大型機を電池で飛ばすのは重すぎて現実的でないため、SAFが最も現実的な手段とされています。

qs.q: According to the passage, one advantage of SAF is that
o: it can be used in existing aircraft without major changes.
it releases no carbon dioxide when it is burned.
it is cheaper than conventional jet fuel.
it can be made only from fresh vegetables.
qs.ex: can be mixed with regular fuel and used in existing aircraft とあります。燃焼時のCO2は通常燃料と同程度です。

qs.q: What is the main problem with SAF today?
o: Airlines do not know how to use it.
Governments have banned it at some airports.
It is expensive, and there are not enough raw materials.
qs.ex: The biggest obstacle is cost ... and the supply of suitable raw materials is limited とあります。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: The Power of Citizen Science
blocks.body:
Scientific research has traditionally been carried out by trained professionals working in universities and laboratories. In recent years, however, ordinary people have been making significant contributions through what is known as citizen science. By collecting data, sharing observations, and analyzing images on their computers or smartphones, volunteers around the world are helping scientists answer questions that would be impossible to study otherwise.
One of the best-known examples is eBird, a project started in 2002 by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology in the United States. Birdwatchers record which species they see, along with the time and location, and upload the information to a shared online database. Over the years, the project has collected well over a billion observations. With so much data from so many places, researchers can track how bird populations change and how migration routes shift in response to factors such as climate change, something that a small team of scientists could never do alone.
Citizen science also benefits the volunteers themselves. Many participants say that they have learned to pay closer attention to nature and feel more connected to their communities. Some projects are designed for schools, allowing students to experience real scientific research rather than simply reading about it in textbooks.
Nevertheless, citizen science has its critics. Some scientists worry about the quality of data collected by people without formal training. A beginner might misidentify a bird, for example, or forget to record important details. To address these concerns, many projects use automatic filters that flag unusual reports, and experienced volunteers review the records. Researchers also use statistical methods to account for differences in observers' skills. Thanks to such measures, citizen science is increasingly accepted as a valuable part of modern research.

qs.q: What is one reason eBird has been valuable to researchers?
o: It is run entirely by professional scientists.
It replaced the need for university research.
It provides a huge amount of data from many locations.
It pays birdwatchers to record their observations.
qs.ex: 多くの場所からの大量のデータで、少人数の研究者ではできない分析ができます。

qs.q: According to the passage, how do volunteers benefit from citizen science?
o: They often feel more connected to nature and their communities.
qs.ex: pay closer attention to nature and feel more connected to their communities とあります。

qs.q: What concern do some scientists have about citizen science?
o: The data may be less accurate.
It takes too much time to organize.
It may replace school science classes.
qs.ex: 専門的な訓練を受けていない人のデータの質を心配しています。

qs.q: How do projects try to deal with the concern mentioned above?
o: By allowing only professionals to submit data.
By limiting the number of volunteers.
By paying for expensive training courses.
By using automatic filters and having records reviewed.
qs.ex: automatic filters ... and experienced volunteers review the records とあります。

parts.prompt:
以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。
語数の目安は60語〜70語です。
parts.body:
Cultivated meat, sometimes called lab-grown meat, is produced by growing animal cells in large steel tanks instead of raising and slaughtering animals. A small sample of cells is taken from a living animal and given nutrients so that it multiplies. Several companies have already received permission to sell such products in some countries.
Supporters argue that cultivated meat could solve several problems at once. Because it does not require raising animals, it could greatly reduce animal suffering. It may also use far less land and water than traditional farming, which would allow forests and other natural areas to be protected.
However, there are still major challenges. At present, producing cultivated meat is extremely expensive, and it is unclear whether the price can be lowered enough for ordinary shoppers. Moreover, the process requires a great deal of energy, so its environmental benefits depend on whether that energy comes from clean sources. Finally, many consumers say they feel uncomfortable eating meat made in a factory, which could limit demand.
rules: 解答は、英文要約の解答欄に書きなさい。なお、解答欄の外に書かれたものは採点されません。
要約の内容が英文から逸れていると判断された場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。英文をよく読んでから答えてください。
parts.model: Cultivated meat is made by growing animal cells in steel tanks rather than by raising animals, and some countries already allow its sale. Supporters say it could reduce animal suffering and use less land and water. However, it is currently very expensive and needs a lot of energy, which may limit its environmental benefits. In addition, many consumers feel uncomfortable eating it.
checks: 培養肉とは何か(細胞を育てて作る・販売が始まっている)が入っている
支持する理由(動物の苦痛・土地や水の節約)が入っている
課題(費用・エネルギー・消費者の抵抗感)が入っている
本文をそのまま写さず、言いかえて短くまとめている
語数が60〜70語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英文要約)

parts.prompt:
以下のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。
POINTSは理由を書く際の参考となる観点を示したものです。ただし、これら以外の観点から理由を書いてもかまいません。

TOPIC
Should governments do more to encourage people to use public transportation?

POINTS
・Cost
・The environment
・Convenience
・Traffic congestion
rules: 語数の目安は120語〜150語です。
構成は、序論・本論・結論が望ましい。
TOPICに示された問いに答えていない場合や、内容がTOPICからずれている場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。
parts.model:
I believe that governments should do more to encourage people to use public transportation, for two main reasons.
First, it would benefit the environment. Cars are a major source of carbon dioxide emissions, and a single bus or train can carry dozens of people while producing far less pollution per passenger. If governments offered discounted fares or improved services, more people would leave their cars at home, helping to slow climate change.
Second, it would reduce traffic congestion. In many cities, traffic jams waste huge amounts of time and fuel every day. When more commuters use trains and buses, roads become less crowded, which allows emergency vehicles and delivery trucks to move more smoothly.
In conclusion, because greater use of public transportation would protect the environment and ease congestion, governments should actively promote it.
checks: 序論で自分の立場(賛成/反対)をはっきり述べている
POINTSなどを使った理由を2つ、具体例とともに書いている
本論の各段落が First / Second で始まり、構成がわかる
結論で立場と理由をまとめ直している
語数が120〜150語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英作文)

lines: Hey, Tom, did you get the email about the new expense system?
Yeah. I tried to submit my travel receipts last night, but the app kept crashing.
Same here. I ended up calling IT. They said there's a bug they're fixing, and we should use the old paper forms until Friday.
Paper forms? I thought they got rid of those.
Apparently not. They're in the cabinet by the printer.
items.q: What will the man probably do?
o: Wait until Friday to submit his receipts.
items.ex: 金曜まで紙の書類を使うよう言われ、場所も教えてもらっています。

lines: Honey, have you decided which summer camp to send Emily to?
I'm leaning toward the science camp. She's been talking about robots nonstop.
It's twice as expensive as the swimming camp, though.
I know, but the swimming camp is only in the mornings, so one of us would have to leave work early every day.
Good point. Let's go with the science camp, then.
items.q: Why do they choose the science camp?
o: It is closer to their home.
items.ex: 水泳キャンプは午前のみで仕事を早退する必要があるため、一日中のサイエンスキャンプを選びました。

lines: Excuse me. I'm supposed to be on the 6:40 flight to Denver, but the board says it's been canceled.
Yes, ma'am, due to a mechanical problem. I can put you on the 9:15 flight tonight, or the first flight tomorrow at 7 a.m.

lines: How's the job search going, Mia?
Not great. I've had three interviews, but no offers.
Have you asked the companies for feedback?
No. I assumed they wouldn't tell me anything.
You'd be surprised. When I was looking, one company told me my answers were too vague. It really helped.
Maybe I'll email the last one, then.
items.q: What does the man suggest Mia do?
items.ex: 面接した会社に意見を聞くことを勧めています。

lines: The landlord just called. He's going to raise our rent by ten percent next year.
I know. Should we start looking for another place?
Moving costs a lot, too. Let's talk to him first. Maybe he'll agree to five percent if we sign a two-year lease.
items.q: What does the man want to do first?
items.ex: まず大家と話して値上げ幅を下げてもらう交渉をしたいと考えています。

lines: Ms. Chen, the results of your blood test look fine, but your blood pressure is a little high.
Not yet, but I'd recommend cutting down on salt and getting more exercise. Let's check it again in three months.
items.q: What does the doctor recommend?
items.ex: cutting down on salt and getting more exercise と勧めています。薬は今は不要です。

lines: Did you hear that the company is moving its headquarters to Osaka?
Yeah. I'm not sure what to do. My wife just started a new job here in Tokyo.
They said employees can work remotely three days a week.
That might help, but I'd still have to be in Osaka twice a week. I think I'll ask about transferring to the Tokyo branch office.
items.q: What is the man going to do?
o: Move to Osaka with his family.
Ask about working at the Tokyo branch.
Work remotely five days a week.
items.ex: 東京支社への異動について聞いてみるつもりです。

lines: I'm thinking of getting an electric car, but I'm worried about charging.
No, I park on the street.
That could be a problem. Is there a charging station near your apartment?
The closest one is about two kilometers away.
Then maybe a hybrid would make more sense for now.
items.q: What does the woman suggest?
items.ex: 充電が不便なので、今はハイブリッド車のほうがよいと言っています。

lines: Professor Grant, I was wondering if I could get an extension on my research paper.
I've been sick with the flu for the past week. I have a note from my doctor.
All right. You can submit it next Friday, but no later.
items.q: Why does the student ask for an extension?
items.ex: 1週間インフルエンザだったからです。

I want to, but I have to finish the quarterly report.
My boss needs it first thing in the morning.
Well, the party starts at seven. Maybe you can drop by after you're done.
items.q: Why might the woman miss the party?
o: Her boss is coming to the party.
She has to finish a report.
items.ex: 明朝までに報告書を仕上げる必要があります。

lines: This restaurant has terrible reviews online, you know.
Really? My coworker said it was great.
People say the service is slow and the portions are small.
Well, reviews aren't always reliable. Let's try it and see for ourselves. If it's bad, we can grab a pizza on the way home.
items.q: What does the man think about online reviews?
o: They should be written by experts.
They are useful for choosing pizza.
items.ex: reviews aren't always reliable と言っています。

lines: Hi. I'd like to cancel my gym membership.
I'm moving to another city next month.
I see. Actually, we have branches in most major cities. You could transfer your membership instead.
Oh, I didn't know that. Is there one in Sendai?
items.q: What will the man probably do?
items.ex: 引っ越し先の仙台にも支店があるので、会員を移すと考えられます。

lines: The Benefits of Boredom. Most people try to avoid boredom, but some psychologists believe that it can actually be useful. In one study, participants were first asked to do a dull task: copying numbers from a telephone directory. Afterward, they were asked to think of as many uses as possible for a pair of plastic cups. Compared with participants who had not done the boring task, they came up with more creative ideas. Researchers suggest that when we are bored, our minds begin to wander, which can help us make new connections. For this reason, some experts recommend that people put away their smartphones from time to time and allow themselves to feel bored.

o: People who were bored did worse on the second task.
People who had done a boring task gave more creative ideas.
Using smartphones makes people more creative.
qs.ex: 退屈な作業をした人のほうが、コップの使い道をより創造的に考えました。

o: Doing boring tasks at work every day.
Avoiding boredom as much as possible.
qs.ex: put away their smartphones from time to time と勧めています。

items.title: The Benefits of Boredom

lines: Plastic-Eating Bacteria. In 2016, a team of Japanese scientists reported an unusual discovery. While examining samples from a plastic bottle recycling facility, they found a type of bacteria that could break down PET, the plastic used to make many drink bottles. The bacteria produce enzymes that cut the plastic into smaller pieces, which they then use as food. Since the discovery, researchers around the world have been modifying these enzymes to make them work faster. However, the process is still too slow and expensive to use on a large scale, so it will likely be many years before it can make a real difference to the world's plastic waste problem.

o: At a plastic bottle recycling facility.
qs.ex: ペットボトルのリサイクル施設のサンプルから見つかりました。

qs.q: What is one problem with using the bacteria?
o: The process is still too slow and expensive.
They cannot survive outside a laboratory.
qs.ex: the process is still too slow and expensive to use on a large scale とあります。

items.title: Plastic-Eating Bacteria

lines: Daylight Saving Time. Daylight saving time, the practice of moving clocks forward by one hour in spring, was first adopted nationally by Germany in 1916 to save fuel during World War I. Many other countries later followed. The idea was that people would use less electricity for lighting in the evening. Today, however, the energy savings are thought to be small, and the system has become controversial. Some studies have found that the number of heart attacks and traffic accidents rises slightly in the days after clocks are moved forward, possibly because people lose an hour of sleep. As a result, several countries and regions have debated whether to stop changing their clocks altogether.

qs.q: Why was daylight saving time first adopted?
o: To save fuel during a war.
qs.ex: 第一次世界大戦中に燃料を節約するためでした。

qs.q: According to some studies, what happens after clocks are moved forward?
o: Heart attacks and traffic accidents increase slightly.
qs.ex: 心臓発作や交通事故がわずかに増えるという研究があります。

items.title: Daylight Saving Time

lines: The Rosetta Stone. In 1799, French soldiers in Egypt discovered a large stone with writing carved into it. The stone contained the same message written in three different scripts: Egyptian hieroglyphs, a later Egyptian script called Demotic, and ancient Greek. At the time, no one could read hieroglyphs, but many scholars could read ancient Greek. By comparing the three versions, researchers were able to begin understanding the hieroglyphs. In 1822, the French scholar Jean-François Champollion announced that he had worked out how the writing system functioned. His breakthrough allowed historians to read thousands of ancient Egyptian texts for the first time.

qs.q: Why was the Rosetta Stone so important?
o: It was the largest stone ever found in Egypt.
It had the same text in a script scholars could already read.
It showed a map of ancient Egypt.
It was made by a famous French artist.
qs.ex: 学者が読める古代ギリシャ語と同じ内容が書かれていたため、比較できました。

o: He discovered the stone in Egypt.
He translated the Greek text into French.
He worked out how hieroglyphs functioned.
He brought the stone to France.
qs.ex: ヒエログリフのしくみを解明したと発表しました。

items.title: The Rosetta Stone

lines: Urban Beekeeping. In recent years, beekeeping has become popular in cities such as London, Paris, and Tokyo. People keep beehives on the roofs of office buildings, hotels, and even department stores. Surprisingly, bees often do well in cities because parks, gardens, and street trees provide a wide variety of flowers, and fewer chemicals are used than on many farms. However, some ecologists have raised concerns. They point out that if too many honeybee hives are placed in one area, the honeybees may compete with wild bees and other insects for the same flowers. They suggest that cities should plant more flowers before adding more hives.

qs.q: Why do bees often do well in cities?
o: There are fewer birds that eat them.
Beekeepers feed them sugar every day.
Cities offer many kinds of flowers and fewer chemicals.
qs.ex: 多様な花があり、農地より化学物質が少ないからです。

o: Planting more flowers before adding more hives.
Keeping only wild bees on roofs.
qs.ex: cities should plant more flowers before adding more hives とあります。

items.title: Urban Beekeeping

lines: A Bird-Inspired Train. When Japan's high-speed trains entered tunnels at great speed, they created a loud boom at the other end, caused by air being pushed out of the tunnel. An engineer working on a new train in the 1990s, who was also a keen birdwatcher, thought about the kingfisher. This bird dives from the air into water with very little splash, thanks to the long, narrow shape of its beak. The engineer's team designed the front of the train to imitate this shape. The new design greatly reduced the noise in tunnels, and the train was also reported to use less electricity while traveling faster than earlier models.

qs.q: What problem did the engineer want to solve?
o: Trains were using too much fuel.
Trains caused a loud boom when leaving tunnels.
qs.ex: トンネルを出るときの大きな音を減らしたかったのです。

qs.q: Why did the engineer think about the kingfisher?
o: It can fly faster than other birds.
It enters water with very little splash.
qs.ex: カワセミはくちばしの形のおかげで、水に飛び込んでもほとんど水しぶきが立ちません。

items.title: A Bird-Inspired Train

lines: Sure, let me tell you about our most popular models. The Swift X is our lightest laptop at just 1 kilogram, but it's 1,200 dollars. The Nova 14 weighs 1.3 kilograms and costs 850 dollars, and it's very popular with students. The Titan Pro is the most powerful, but it weighs 2.5 kilograms and costs 950 dollars.
